channel.title: Daily Recap — 💾 Apple News
channel.description: What happened in 💾 Apple News, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: Apple's 'Welcome home' event is tomorrow: three new products coming
item.description:
Apple confirmed its "Welcome home" event kicks off tomorrow (October 13), with three new products expected: a trio of new Macs and a new iPad Mini. Reporting suggests a two-day showcase format in Los Angeles, which is unusual for Apple and signals a bigger story than a press-release drop.

Separate reporting details five big upgrades coming to a new Apple TV 4K launching this week, M6 MacBook Pro upgrades arriving later this month, and a broader look at when the rest of Apple's 2026 hardware — HomeView, OLED MacBook Pro, and more — is shipping. After a quiet summer, Apple is ending the year with a packed release calendar.

item.title: iPhone Duo: pre-orders open, orders reportedly up 30%
item.description:
You can now start the iPhone Duo pre-order process ahead of Friday's launch — Apple's setup tool lets you get checkout ready in advance. Multiple outlets report Apple has increased iPhone Duo production orders by about 30 percent, a strong demand signal for the foldable.

Deep dives this week also revealed clever engineering: the Duo's hinge hides a cooling system designed to give it desktop-like performance, and Apple detailed where its engineers focused to make that possible. Demand is there; now the hinge has to hold up in the real world.

Sources

item.title: iPhone hits record Q3 shipment share as the global market plunges
item.description:
The iPhone captured a record Q3 share of global smartphone shipments even as the overall market plunged 20 percent, according to a new report. Counterpoint-style data shows Apple trailing Samsung in absolute shipments but winning share — a premium-market story that keeps playing out in downturns.

Wall Street is split on what comes next: JP Morgan hiked its AAPL price target to $360 while dismissing recent iPhone production-cut reports. Either demand is fine, or the cuts were never real; either way, the analyst community is pricing in a strong holiday quarter.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: iPhone hits record Q3 shipment share as global smartphone market plunges 20%, per report
  • AppleInsider News: Apple trails Samsung as global smartphone shipments hit a 13-year low
  • 9to5Mac: Apple gets a $360 price target from JP Morgan despite iPhone demand concerns

item.title: App Store 'Indie Games Week' kicks off; No Man's Sky comes to iPhone and iPad
item.description:
Apple launched "Indie Games Week" on the App Store, spotlighting six new iPhone and iPad games plus seven upcoming launches. It's the biggest indie push the App Store has made in a while, and it comes with a headliner: No Man's Sky is coming to iPhone and iPad, essentially the full game on mobile.

For Apple, this is about answering the gaming question — the M-series chips are overkill for the mobile game library, and marquee ports like this are how Apple convinces developers the platform is serious.

Sources

item.title: Beats x Pokémon Pill speaker, Tim Cook's third China trip, and more
item.description:
Beats and Pokémon teased a special Pikachu-themed Pill speaker collaboration — a nostalgia play aimed squarely at a generation that grew up with both brands. Details are thin, but the teaser confirms it's real.

Meanwhile, Tim Cook visited China for the third time this year, underscoring how central the market and supply chain remain despite geopolitical noise. And in smaller news: Apple launched a special-edition AirPods 5 in India, OLED iPad Mini rumors point to a $200 price bump, and Apple kicked off a "Switch to Safari" campaign arguing you should ditch Chrome.

item.title: Apple vs. Epic flares up again in court
item.description:
The Apple-Epic fight isn't over: a new joint filing shows Epic remains unhappy with Apple "at every turn," and the two sides clashed over document production in the latest App Store court filing. Years after the original verdict, compliance and enforcement are still being litigated.

The stakes are bigger than one case — every skirmish in this saga sets precedent for how app store rules get enforced globally. Expect more rounds.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: New joint filing shows Epic remains unhappy with Apple at every turn
  • 9to5Mac: Apple and Epic clash over document production in latest App Store court filing

item.title: Apple's smart home hub is called 'HomeView,' ships mid-November in four colors
item.description:
The biggest pre-event leak: Apple's smart-home hub will be called HomeView, ship in mid-November in four colors, and run on an A18 chip, per MacRumors and 9to5Mac. Six Colors confirms the name and frames it as the centerpiece of Tuesday's 'Welcome Home' event.

AppleInsider adds that ADT is rumored to handle installations — a smart move that gives Apple a professional-install story on day one instead of asking the Hub to bootstrap an ecosystem alone. The question hanging over all of it: is this finally Apple's first real smart-home success?

item.title: Apple TV 4K gets A19 chip, easier-to-find Siri Remote, possible built-in mic
item.description:
MacRumors reports the new Apple TV 4K will get an A19 chip and a Siri Remote that's easier to find — likely meaning speaker/UWB tracking. AppleInsider and 9to5Mac add that the box itself might have microphones, and both the Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini are expected to ship October 30.

MacRumors' roundup collects 16 leaked details across the Apple TV, HomeView, and HomePod Mini. The through-line: Apple is treating the living room as a platform again, not an accessory.

item.title: What to expect at Tuesday's 'Welcome Home' event
item.description:
AppleInsider and The Verge both published event previews ahead of the October 13 'Welcome Home' releases. Expect the HomeView hub, HomePod Mini 2, and Apple TV 4K to headline, with the smart-home angle tying everything together.

TechCrunch asks the sharper question — will HomeView be Apple's first smart-home success? — while Techmeme looks at the broader strategy centered on the hub display. After years of HomeKit half-measures, Tuesday is Apple's put-up-or-shut-up moment in the home.

Sources

  • AppleInsider: What to expect from Apple's October 13 'Welcome home' releases

item.title: iPhone Duo gets huge retail showcases — but supply will be limited
item.description:
MacRumors reports Apple is planning major iPhone Duo retail demo experiences at select stores, with 9to5Mac adding detail on the in-store push. The catch: supply will be limited at launch.

Big experiential retail plus constrained supply is a familiar Apple playbook — it worked for Vision Pro — and suggests the Duo is positioned as a halo product rather than a volume play, at least initially.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Plans Major iPhone Duo Retail Showcase, But Supply Will Be Limited
  • 9to5Mac: Apple planning huge iPhone Duo demo experiences at select retail stores: report

item.title: iPad outlook: no new entry-level model until 2027; OLED iPad mini will be pricey
item.description:
AppleInsider and MacRumors report the updated entry-level iPad won't arrive until early 2027 — a long wait that suggests Apple is holding the line on its current lineup through the holidays.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg via 9to5Mac says the OLED iPad mini will be 'significantly more expensive' than the current model. OLED is a real upgrade, but the mini has always sold on value — a big price jump could test that.

item.title: MacBook Pro overhaul coming sooner than expected for the entry model
item.description:
9to5Mac reports the MacBook Pro overhaul is coming, with the entry-level model gaining the new design sooner than expected. AppleInsider's Sunday Reboot column wishes aloud for macOS on iPad instead — the perennial dream that refuses to die.

On the deals front, MacRumors spots up to $200 off the Mac Mini and Mac Studio at Amazon, plus AirPods Max 2 for $429 in all colors.

item.title: Tim Cook in China for the third time this year; iOS 27 rollout was oddly quiet
item.description:
AppleInsider notes Tim Cook is visiting China for the third time in 2026 — a frequency that underscores how critical the market remains amid ongoing supply-chain and regulatory pressures.

Daring Fireball observes Apple only started suggesting iOS 26 users upgrade to 27 three days ago, an unusually quiet rollout for a major release. And in fun news, AppleInsider found a vibe-coded Adobe Creative Suite clone that's 'pretty good' — the vibe-coding era claims another victim.

item.title: Apple's 'Welcome Home' event is Tuesday: Home Hub, HomePod Mini 2, new Apple TV 4K
item.description:
Apple's October 13 'Welcome Home' event is shaping up as the company's biggest smart-home moment in years. MacRumors reports the headliner is an all-new Home Hub — a brand-new device category for Apple, not just another speaker — joined by a HomePod Mini 2 with new features and a long-overdue Apple TV 4K refresh.

Six Colors zooms out to ask whether Apple is 'coming home to stay,' arguing this event signals a serious renewed push into the home after years of half-hearted dabbling with HomeKit. If the Hub lands, it would be Apple's first truly new product category since the Vision Pro — with very different stakes. MacRumors' Top Stories roundup collects everything expected so you can walk into Tuesday fully briefed.

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro orders reportedly cut; iPhone Duo will greet owners by name
item.description:
Supply-chain sources claim Apple has cut iPhone 18 Pro orders 'right on schedule' — a rumor that surfaces nearly every iPhone cycle, usually says more about seasonal production adjustments than actual demand, and should be taken with the usual skepticism until sales data arrives.

More concrete: AppleInsider found that the iPhone Duo will greet some owners by name on first boot, a small personal touch in the setup experience that hints at how Apple is thinking about first-run personalization going forward.

Sources

  • AppleInsider: Right on schedule, sources claim iPhone 18 Pro orders have been cut
  • AppleInsider: iPhone Duo will greet some owners by name on its first boot

item.title: Amazon's Alexa Tablet finally gives the iPad real competition
item.description:
9to5Mac argues Amazon's new Alexa Tablet is the first credible iPad challenger in years — and the threat is real precisely because it doesn't try to beat the iPad at Apple's game. Instead it attacks from below with aggressive pricing and an Alexa-first experience.

No Android tablet has managed sustained pressure on the iPad, but Amazon's content ecosystem and smart-home integration give this one a different angle. If it sells, expect Apple to feel pressure to defend the low end of the lineup rather than ceding it entirely.

item.title: Weekend deals: $430 off MacBook Pro M5 Pro, plus AirPods and accessory sales
item.description:
A strong weekend for Apple deals. AppleInsider spots $430 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro, bringing it to $2,069 — one of the steepest discounts on current-gen Pro hardware.

MacRumors rounds up weekend accessory deals spanning TVs, headphones, and smart home gear, while 9to5Mac lists Apple's own weekend sales: AirPods, up to $200 off new Macs, and Apple Watch starting from $41. If you've been waiting on any of these, this is a genuine buy window, not the usual token $20 off.

item.title: Rumor: Apple to announce new partnership with ADT
item.description:
MacRumors reports Apple is set to announce a new partnership with home-security company ADT. Details are thin, but the timing — days before the 'Welcome Home' event — is conspicuous.

An ADT tie-up would give Apple's smart-home push an installed base and professional-monitoring story on day one, rather than asking the Home Hub to bootstrap an ecosystem alone. Expect more partnerships like this if Apple is serious about the home.

Sources

item.title: Odds and ends: 30 Mac minis vs. a Cray-1, macOS 27's underrated IT win, AirPods 5 guide
item.description:
AppleInsider notes that 30 old Intel Mac minis stuffed into a Cray-1 chassis are hugely faster than the supercomputer they live in — a fun reminder of how far commodity computing has come.

For the IT crowd, 9to5Mac highlights remote AppleCare log collection as one of macOS 27's most underrated updates, and its Indie App Spotlight covers Milepost, a driving journal that saves memories from the road. MacRumors also published an AirPods 5 buyer's guide comparing the standard model against the wireless-charging-case version.
